From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-12T07:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: unusual error spike on transactions endpoint

Quick update from infra: observing a correlated increase in queue latency on the us-west cluster starting 07:18 PT. P99 token latency up from ~120ms to ~1.8s for a subset of shortest-sequence requests. 502s appear tied to gateway timeouts during backend batching windows.

What we have so far:
- Root cause hypothesis: an unseen load pattern (burst of many short requests) caused batching to grow and TTLs to be exceeded at the proxy layer; also noticed elevated GC churn on one replica set.
- Action taken: kicked a rolling drain on suspect node group, increased frontend proxy timeout to 6s as short-term mitigation, and disabled a new experimental batching threshold that was active on a canary.
- Attached: p99_latency_plot.png and initial request samples (request_logs_20260812.gz).

Next:
- Continue rolling drains across the pool (ongoing, ETA 40m).
- We will open a dedicated tracing span filter for Delta’s API key to capture fine-grained timelines (ETA 15m).

Jonas Weber
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: p99_latency_plot.png (image), request_logs_20260812.gz (gzip)

Hi Samir / Heather — quick status update from Redwood:

What we see now:
- Starting ~07:18 PT there was a spike in p99 latency and a corresponding rise in 502s for a subset of traffic routed to our us-west serving pool.
- Our engineering team has identified a likely batching/timeout interaction and is performing rolling drains and temporary proxy timeout increases as mitigations.

What we are doing now:
- Rolling drains across the affected nodes (ongoing).
- Capturing per-request traces for Delta traffic to nail down tail latency contributors (ETA 30–45m).
- Preparing a short RCA and next steps once we confirm root cause.

Expected next update: 30–45 minutes or sooner if we observe customer-facing recovery. We understand the sale is time-sensitive and are prioritizing this.

If you’d like a private bridge, we can open one now and invite engineering — please reply and I’ll send a link.

Subject: Delta Payments — resolution and next steps

Hi Samir / Heather — following up with final update.

Summary: the customer-facing impact resolved at ~14:50 PT after rolling drains and reverting the experimental batching threshold. Root cause: an interaction between a canary batching optimization and the proxy timeout configuration that caused larger-than-expected batch formation and gateway timeouts for short requests.

What we did:
- Reverted the canary batching threshold across all serving pools.
- Increased proxy timeouts temporarily during mitigation.
- Performed rolling drains and validated healthy host-level GC metrics.
- Captured full traces for Delta traffic and saved request samples for post-mortem.

Customer impact: approx 18% of checkout requests saw timeouts between 07:18–14:50 PT. We sincerely apologize for the disruption to your flash sale.

Next steps (deliverables):
- Full RCA and mitigation timeline by EOD tomorrow (08/13).
- Proposed customer credit range for internal review (Marcus will lead).
- Follow-up call with Delta engineering & product to review technical details and validation (Propose 08/13 10:00 PT).

If you’d like that follow-up call, I can schedule and include our SRE and product leads.

Thanks for your patience — we know this was consequential and we’re committed to a thorough post-incident review.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
